title: Dichromate ion
back: Two $\ce{CrO4}$ tetrahedra sharing one O; Cr–O–Cr ≈ 126°; Cr in +6. Orange; chromate (yellow) in alkali.

title: Permanganate ion
back: Tetrahedral, Mn +7, $d^0$: purple from charge transfer, diamagnetic. Manganate ($\ce{MnO4^2-}$) is green and paramagnetic.

title: Permanganate in acid
back: Five electrons; purple → colourless, so it is its own indicator. Acidify with dilute $\ce{H2SO4}$, never HCl.

title: Chromite → potassium dichromate
back: Fuse with sodium carbonate in air, acidify, then add KCl.

title: Pyrolusite → potassium permanganate
back: Fuse to green manganate, then disproportionate in acid or oxidise electrolytically to purple permanganate.

title: Lanthanoid contraction
back: Consequences: Zr and Hf have almost the same radius; lanthanoids are hard to separate; basicity falls from La(OH)₃ to Lu(OH)₃.

title: Lanthanoids vs actinoids
back: Actinoids: more oxidation states, all radioactive, form oxo ions, stronger complexes, larger contraction.

title: A handful and an over
back: Permanganate takes 5 electrons in acid (a hand); dichromate takes 6 (a cricket over).
